blocks.text: Teen Driving Lessons
Teen Driving Lessons page →
How much are driving lessons for teens?
heading_path: How much are driving lessons for teens?

blocks.text: Teen pricing depends on the program. Behind-the-Wheel Only training is $350, and the complete Teen 24-Hour Classroom & Driving package is $399. Online-only driver education is priced separately — call (469) 709-7613 for current pricing and what each package includes.
heading_path: How much are driving lessons for teens?

blocks.text: How much is the teen driving lesson for 6 hours?
heading_path: How much is the teen driving lesson for 6 hours?

blocks.text: Teen behind-the-wheel packages follow Texas’s required 7 hours of driving plus 7 hours of observation rather than a standalone 6-hour block. If you need a specific number of in-car hours, call us and we’ll match you to the right package.
heading_path: How much is the teen driving lesson for 6 hours?

blocks.text: Can a teen take driving lessons with a Learner Permit?
heading_path: Can a teen take driving lessons with a Learner Permit?

blocks.text: Yes. A valid Texas Learner License is required before behind-the-wheel training begins. Once your teen holds a permit and meets enrollment requirements, they can start in-car lessons with a licensed instructor.
heading_path: Can a teen take driving lessons with a Learner Permit?

blocks.text: What is required for a Texas Learner Permit?
heading_path: What is required for a Texas Learner Permit?

blocks.text: Texas DPS sets Learner License eligibility and documentation requirements, which typically include proof of identity, driver education enrollment or completion, and passing the knowledge test. Always review the current Texas DPS checklist before your appointment.
heading_path: What is required for a Texas Learner Permit?

blocks.text: Can my teen take behind-the-wheel lessons after completing online driver education somewhere else?
heading_path: Can my teen take behind-the-wheel lessons after completing online driver education somewhere else?

blocks.text: Yes. Our Teen Behind-the-Wheel Only option is built for students who have completed — or are completing — an accepted driver education course elsewhere and now need professional in-car instruction. Bring your driver education records so we can confirm eligibility.
heading_path: Can my teen take behind-the-wheel lessons after completing online driver education somewhere else?

heading_path: Can an adult take driving lessons with no previous experience?

blocks.text: Parent-Taught Log Driving
Parent-Taught Log Driving page →
What is parent-taught log driving?

Parent-Taught Driver Education (PTDE) allows an eligible Parent Instructor to guide a teen through an approved Texas driver education program. Parents supervise practice and maintain the required Driving Log.
How many parent taught driving hours are required in Texas?
heading_path: How many parent taught driving hours are required in Texas?

blocks.text: The exact number of logged hours depends on the approved course and current TDLR requirements. Best Driving School offers 30-hour, 15-hour, and 10-hour professional instruction options — call to confirm current requirements.
heading_path: How many parent taught driving hours are required in Texas?

blocks.text: Who can act as the Parent Instructor?
heading_path: Who can act as the Parent Instructor?

blocks.text: The Parent Instructor is the parent or eligible guardian who qualifies under the approved course to teach the curriculum, supervise practice, maintain records, and sign required documents.
heading_path: Who can act as the Parent Instructor?

blocks.text: Does my teen need a Learner License before driving?
heading_path: Does my teen need a Learner License before driving?

blocks.text: Yes. The student completes the educational phase, then follows current Texas DPS requirements to obtain a Learner License before behind-the-wheel practice begins.
heading_path: Does my teen need a Learner License before driving?

blocks.text: Can Best Driving School help with the parent taught driving log?
heading_path: Can Best Driving School help with the parent taught driving log?

blocks.text: Yes. We can help families understand how professional lessons relate to the driving log. The authorized Parent Instructor remains responsible for maintaining and certifying the records.
heading_path: Can Best Driving School help with the parent taught driving log?

blocks.text: Can professional lessons count toward supervised driving hours?
heading_path: Can professional lessons count toward supervised driving hours?

blocks.text: Professional behind-the-wheel training supports the parent-taught process. Confirm with your approved course provider and current TDLR guidance how professional lesson hours apply to logged practice.
heading_path: Can professional lessons count toward supervised driving hours?

heading_path: Can a parent-taught student take the Road Test at a driving school?

heading_path: Can a parent-taught student take the Road Test at a driving school?

heading_path: Are parent-taught driving lessons available in Plano, Allen, Frisco and McKinney?

blocks.text: Yes. Best Driving School supports Parent-Taught Driver Education families across Plano, Allen, Frisco, McKinney, and surrounding North Texas communities.

blocks.text: 3rd-Party Road Test
3rd-Party Road Test page →
What is a 3rd party road test in Texas?
heading_path: What is a 3rd party road test in Texas?

blocks.text: It is the official Texas Class C non-commercial driving skills examination, administered by a DPS-authorized driving school instead of a DPS office. Passing it has the same licensing value as passing the test at DPS.
heading_path: What is a 3rd party road test in Texas?

blocks.text: Is a 3rd party road test the same as the DPS road test?
heading_path: Is a 3rd party road test the same as the DPS road test?

blocks.text: Yes. A person who passes through a DPS-authorized 3rd party testing provider receives the same type of Texas driver license as an applicant who passes at a DPS office. There is no separate “third party” license.
heading_path: Is a 3rd party road test the same as the DPS road test?

blocks.text: Who is eligible to take the 3rd party road test at Best Driving School in Plano?
heading_path: Who is eligible to take the 3rd party road test at Best Driving School in Plano?

blocks.text: Eligibility depends on age, driver education history, current restricted license, and Impact Texas Drivers certificate. This generally covers teen drivers ages 16–17 and adults age 18 and over.
heading_path: Who is eligible to take the 3rd party road test at Best Driving School in Plano?

blocks.text: What documents do I need to bring to the road test?
heading_path: What documents do I need to bring to the road test?

blocks.text: Requirements vary by age group, but generally include a valid Texas Learner License or restricted license, the correct driver education certificate, a printed Impact Texas Drivers certificate dated within 90 days, and printed proof of current liability insurance.
heading_path: What documents do I need to bring to the road test?

blocks.text: What happens if I fail the road test?
heading_path: What happens if I fail the road test?

blocks.text: The Road Test and Practice and Road Test services do not guarantee a passing result. If you are not successful, additional driving lessons can help you build the skills needed before scheduling another attempt.
heading_path: What happens if I fail the road test?

blocks.text: How long does it take to get my license after passing at Best Driving School?
heading_path: How long does it take to get my license after passing at Best Driving School?

blocks.text: Processing time varies and is controlled by DPS, not Best Driving School. After DPS reviews the documents, an eligible applicant can complete the transaction, receive a temporary license, and later the permanent card by mail.
heading_path: How long does it take to get my license after passing at Best Driving School?

blocks.text: Do I need to visit a DPS office after passing the road test?
heading_path: Do I need to visit a DPS office after passing the road test?

blocks.text: If Best Driving School submits an eligible application through the DPS Third-Party Skills Testing Submission Portal and DPS approves it, you can complete the licensing payment online without a separate office visit.
heading_path: Do I need to visit a DPS office after passing the road test?

blocks.text: Can I use my own car for the road test?
heading_path: Can I use my own car for the road test?

blocks.text: Applicants are generally responsible for providing the vehicle used during the exam, along with printed proof of current liability insurance for that vehicle. Confirm current vehicle requirements with Best Driving School before your appointment.
heading_path: Can I use my own car for the road test?

blocks.text: What does the Texas road test evaluate?
heading_path: What does the Texas road test evaluate?

blocks.text: The test measures four key driving skills known as the COPS framework: Control, Observation, Position, and Signal.
heading_path: What does the Texas road test evaluate?

blocks.text: Where can I take a 3rd party road test near Allen, Frisco, and McKinney?
heading_path: Where can I take a 3rd party road test near Allen, Frisco, and McKinney?

blocks.text: Best Driving School administers the 3rd party road test at its Plano testing location, 8901 Independence Pkwy Suite 10, Plano, TX 75025, which conveniently serves the surrounding communities.
heading_path: Where can I take a 3rd party road test near Allen, Frisco, and McKinney?

blocks.text: What is the difference between Road Test and Practice and Road Test?
heading_path: What is the difference between Road Test and Practice and Road Test?

blocks.text: Road Test is the official Class C driving skills exam alone. Practice and Road Test adds an instructor-led practice session immediately before the official exam.
heading_path: What is the difference between Road Test and Practice and Road Test?

blocks.text: What happens during the practice portion of Practice and Road Test?
heading_path: What happens during the practice portion of Practice and Road Test?

blocks.text: A licensed instructor reviews parking, backing, complete stops, observation, lane position, signaling, speed control, and right-of-way, and can provide feedback before the official test begins.
heading_path: What happens during the practice portion of Practice and Road Test?

blocks.text: Does Practice and Road Test guarantee that I will pass?
heading_path: Does Practice and Road Test guarantee that I will pass?

blocks.text: No. Practice and Road Test does not guarantee a passing result. It is designed to give you a final professional review immediately before your official, independently-scored road test.
heading_path: Does Practice and Road Test guarantee that I will pass?

blocks.text: Impact Texas Adult Drivers (ITAD)
Is ITAD part of the 6 hours of Driver Education required to complete prior to taking the skills (behind the wheel) examination?
heading_path: Is ITAD part of the 6 hours of Driver Education required to complete prior to taking the skills (behind the wheel) examination?

blocks.text: ITAD is a separate requirement and must be completed no more than 90 days before the applicant takes the skills examination. It is recommended that ITAD be completed after the 6 hour Adult Driver Education Course.
heading_path: Is ITAD part of the 6 hours of Driver Education required to complete prior to taking the skills (behind the wheel) examination?

blocks.text: Who is required to take ITAD?
heading_path: Who is required to take ITAD?

blocks.text: Any applicant who has taken a 6 hour Adult Driver Education Course and was issued an ADE-1317 Certificate must view the ITAD program and receive a completion certificate before the drive test will be administered. The certificate must be dated within 90 days of the drive test. Additionally, applicants ages 18-24 who have been issued a DE-964 showing completion of a Teen Driver Education course (24 hours classroom, 44 hours behind the wheel) are also required to watch the 2 hour ITTD video.
heading_path: Who is required to take ITAD?

blocks.text: Is there an expiration date on the ITAD certificate?
heading_path: Is there an expiration date on the ITAD certificate?

blocks.text: Yes, the ITAD certification has an expiration date. The ITAD certificate is only valid for 90 days. If the applicant does not pass the driving skills examination within 90 days of the date on the certificate, they must restart the ITAD program.
heading_path: Is there an expiration date on the ITAD certificate?

blocks.text: Do I have to watch the 1 hour video in a single viewing?
heading_path: Do I have to watch the 1 hour video in a single viewing?

blocks.text: No, the ITAD video is divided into three (3) modules that can be viewed independently. Each module must be completed in its entirety in order to progress to the next module.
heading_path: Do I have to watch the 1 hour video in a single viewing?

blocks.text: After I complete all modules and finish the ITAD video, how will I receive my certificate?
heading_path: After I complete all modules and finish the ITAD video, how will I receive my certificate?

blocks.text: A copy of the certificate will be emailed to the address used to create an account on the ITAD website. Additionally, you can log in to the ITAD website at any time to retrieve and print your certificate (go to course, course overview, and reprint certificate).
heading_path: After I complete all modules and finish the ITAD video, how will I receive my certificate?
